classification.difficultyReason: Combine a negative population derivative with a positive second derivative to explain a slowing decline, then sketch a decreasing, concave-up curve through the initial population.

content.prompt: The population $P$ of fish in a certain lake was studied over time. At the start of the study the number of fish was 2500.

children.label: a
children.prompt: During the study, $\dfrac{dP}{dt}<0$. What does this say about the number of fish during the study?

answer.short: The number of fish is decreasing.
answer.worked: Since $\dfrac{dP}{dt}<0$, the population decreases as time increases.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If at the same time, $\dfrac{d^2P}{dt^2}>0$, what can you say about the population rate of change?

answer.short: The rate of change is increasing (becoming less negative), so the decline is slowing.
answer.worked: Since $\dfrac{d^2P}{dt^2}>0$, the rate of change $\dfrac{dP}{dt}$ is increasing. It is negative, so it is becoming less negative: the population is decreasing more slowly.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Sketch a possible graph of the population $P$ against $t$.

answer.short: A decreasing, concave-up curve starting at $(0,2500)$ and remaining above the $t$-axis.
answer.worked: The graph starts at $(0,2500)$. Since $\dfrac{dP}{dt}<0$, it slopes downwards. Since $\dfrac{d^2P}{dt^2}>0$, it is concave up and becomes less steep as time increases.

spec.description: Positive population curve beginning at the labelled vertical intercept 2500, decreasing and flattening to the right. Axes have arrowheads and labels P and t; there is no grid.
spec.mathematics: A possible qualitative graph has P(0)=2500, P>0, P'<0 and P''>0. The plotted representative curve expresses these conditions without supplying an equation to students.
